title: Covering Properties of Subset Functions
description: Let X be a finite set of size n. What is the minimum H(n) such that some function f: P(X) -> X covers all of X from any subset Y of size at least H(n)? Known: log₂(n) ≤ H(n) < log₂(n) + O(log log n). Conjecture (OPEN): H(n) - log₂(n) → ∞.

meta.author: Erdős, Hajnal

overview.historicalContext: Erdős and Hajnal (1968) introduced the covering number H(n) in their study of functions on power sets. Given a finite set X of size n, they defined H(n) as the minimum H such that some function f: P(X) → X has the property that {f(A) : A ⊆ Y} = X for every Y ⊆ X with |Y| ≥ H. They proved log₂(n) ≤ H(n) < log₂(n) + (3+o(1))·log₂(log₂(n)) using counting arguments and probabilistic constructions. Noga Alon later proved deep structural results: (1) for any f, some Y of size k has |subsetImage f Y| < (1-c)·2^k (no perfect coverage), and (2) there exist f achieving |subsetImage f Y| > 2^k/4 for all Y (good functions exist). Together these show covering functions are inherently imperfect but can be quite good. The main conjecture that H(n) - log₂(n) → ∞ — and even the weaker statement H(2^k) ≥ k+1 — remain open, making this one of the oldest unsolved problems in combinatorial set theory.
overview.problemStatement:
**Erdős Problem #624** (Erdős-Hajnal, 1968; OPEN):

Let X be a finite set of size n. Define the **covering number** H(n) = min{H : ∃f: P(X)→X, ∀Y⊆X, |Y|≥H → {f(A) : A⊆Y} = X}.

**Known bounds**: log₂(n) ≤ H(n) < log₂(n) + (3+o(1))·log₂(log₂(n))

**Main conjecture**: H(n) - log₂(n) → ∞

**Weaker conjecture** (also OPEN): H(2^k) ≥ k + 1 for all k ≥ 1
overview.text: Let X be a finite set of size n. What is the minimum H(n) such that some function f: P(X) -> X covers all of X from any subset Y of size at least H(n)? Known: log₂(n) ≤ H(n) < log₂(n) + O(log log n). Conjecture (OPEN): H(n) - log₂(n) → ∞.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization proceeds in three layers. First, it defines the core objects: subsetImage f Y = (Y.powerset).image f, the predicate IsCoveringFunction X f H requiring subsetImage f Y = X for all Y ⊆ X with |Y| ≥ H, and coveringNumber X = sInf {H : ℕ | ∃ f, IsCoveringFunction X f H}. Second, it proves basic bounds: |Y.powerset| = 2^|Y| (from Mathlib) and |subsetImage f Y| ≤ 2^|Y| (composing card_image_le with card_powerset). The lower bound argument — if f is H-covering then 2^H ≥ |X| — requires choosing a witness Y ⊆ X with |Y| = H and applying these cardinality bounds (both theorems proved by Aristotle automated proof search). Third, it axiomatizes the deeper results: the Erdős-Hajnal upper bound, the main and weaker conjectures, and Alon's structural theorems on coverage fractions.
keyInsights: The lower bound is a pure counting argument: 2^H subsets of Y can produce at most 2^H distinct images, so covering n elements requires 2^H ≥ n, hence H ≥ log₂(n)
The Erdős-Hajnal upper bound uses the probabilistic method: a random function f achieves H-covering for H < log₂(n) + O(log log n) with positive probability
Alon's results pin down the coverage fraction to between 1/4 and (1-c) of the theoretical maximum 2^k, showing covering functions are inherently imperfect
Even the weaker conjecture H(2^k) ≥ k+1 — that the covering number exceeds log₂(n) by at least 1 at powers of 2 — remains open
The gap between the lower and upper bounds is O(log log n); determining whether this gap is bounded or unbounded is the core open question

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines subsetImage f Y = (Y.powerset).image f, the predicate IsCoveringFunction X f H (universal coverage from all large subsets), and coveringNumber X = sInf over ℕ.
sections.mathContext: Defines subsetImage f Y = (Y.powerset).image f, the predicate IsCoveringFunction X f H (universal coverage from all large subsets), and coveringNumber X = sInf over $\mathbb{N}$.

sections.title: Basic Cardinality Bounds
sections.summary: Proves |Y.powerset| = 2^|Y| (from Mathlib's Finset.card_powerset) and |subsetImage f Y| ≤ 2^|Y| (composing card_image_le with powerset cardinality).
sections.mathContext: Proves |Y.powerset| = 2^|Y| (from Mathlib's Finset.card_powerset) and |subsetImage f Y| $\leq$ 2^|Y| (composing card_image_le with powerset cardinality).

sections.title: Lower Bound: H(n) ≥ log₂(n)
sections.summary: The counting argument: IsCoveringFunction X f H implies 2^H ≥ |X|, hence coveringNumber X ≥ Nat.clog 2 |X|. Both theorems proved by Aristotle automated proof search.
sections.mathContext: The counting argument: IsCoveringFunction X f H implies $2^{H}$ $\geq$ |X|, hence coveringNumber X $\geq$ Nat.clog 2 |X|. Both theorems proved by Aristotle automated proof search.

sections.title: Erdős-Hajnal Upper Bound (1968)
sections.summary: Axiomatized: for n ≥ 4, there exists f and H with IsCoveringFunction X f H and H < log₂(n) + 3·log₂(log₂(n)) + 10. Proved via probabilistic method.
sections.mathContext: Axiomatized: for n $\geq$ 4, there exists f and H with IsCoveringFunction X f H and H < log₂(n) + 3·log₂(log₂(n)) + 10. Proved via probabilistic method.

sections.title: Main Conjecture (OPEN)
sections.summary: States H(n) - log₂(n) → ∞: for all C, there exists N such that for all n > N, coveringNumber X > log₂(n) + C. Axiomatized as erdos_624_open.
sections.mathContext: States H(n) - log₂(n) $\to$ ∞: for all C, there exists N such that for all n > N, coveringNumber X > log₂(n) + C. Axiomatized as erdos_624_open.

sections.title: Weaker Conjecture (Also OPEN)
sections.summary: For n = 2^k, H(n) ≥ k + 1. Strictly weaker than the main conjecture; even this statement that H(n) > log₂(n) at powers of 2 is unproven.
sections.mathContext: For n = $2^{k}$, H(n) $\geq$ k + 1. Strictly weaker than the main conjecture; even this statement that H(n) > log₂(n) at powers of 2 is unproven.

sections.title: Alon's Structural Upper Bound
sections.summary: Axiomatized: ∃ c > 0 such that for any f, some Y ⊆ X with |Y| = k has |subsetImage f Y| < (1-c)·2^k. No function achieves perfect coverage.
sections.mathContext: Axiomatized: ∃ c > 0 such that for any f, some Y ⊆ X with |Y| = k has |subsetImage f Y| < (1-c)·$2^{k}$. No function achieves perfect coverage.

sections.title: Alon's Construction
sections.summary: Axiomatized: for k ≥ 2 and |X| = 2^k, there exists f with |subsetImage f Y| > 2^k/4 for all Y of size k. Good covering functions exist.
sections.mathContext: Axiomatized: for k $\geq$ 2 and |X| = $2^{k}$, there exists f with |subsetImage f Y| > $2^{k}$/4 for all Y of size k. Good covering functions exist.

sections.title: State of Knowledge Summary
sections.summary: Complete picture: log₂(n) + Ω(1) ≤ H(n) < log₂(n) + O(log log n). The gap is between a positive constant (Alon) and O(log log n) (Erdős-Hajnal). Unboundedness is OPEN.
sections.mathContext: Complete picture: log₂(n) + Ω(1) $\leq$ H(n) < log₂(n) + $O(log $\log n$)$. The gap is between a positive constant (Alon) and $O(log $\log n$)$ (Erdős-Hajnal). Unboundedness is OPEN.

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures the complete state of knowledge on Erdős Problem #624. The covering number H(n) — the minimum subset size guaranteeing full coverage under an optimal function — is known to satisfy log₂(n) + Ω(1) ≤ H(n) < log₂(n) + O(log log n). The lower bound counting argument is fully proved (covering_lower_bound and coveringNumber_ge_log completed by Aristotle), while the upper bound and structural results are axiomatized. The main conjecture that H(n) - log₂(n) → ∞ remains one of the oldest open problems in combinatorial set theory.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: Understanding covering numbers connects to coding theory (covering codes), combinatorial optimization, and the structure of functions on power sets.

The question of whether every covering function has inherent inefficiency (Alon's result) has implications for the design of hashing and covering schemes. The O(log log n) gap mirrors similar phenomena in probabilistic combinatorics where random constructions achieve near-optimal bounds.
openQuestions: Main conjecture: prove H(n) - log₂(n) → ∞ (the gap between covering number and logarithmic lower bound is unbounded)
Weaker conjecture: prove H(2^k) ≥ k + 1 (covering number exceeds log₂(n) by at least 1 at powers of 2)
Determine the exact constant c in Alon's structural bound |subsetImage f Y| < (1-c)·2^k
RESOLVED: Both lower bound sorries proved by Aristotle (covering_lower_bound and coveringNumber_ge_log)
